claim: Let \(q=2^m\) with \(m\ge1\), \(k\in\mathbb F_q\), and let \(C_k\subset\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb F_q}\) be the degree-\(q+3\) plane-filling curve \(x^2(x^q y-xy^q)+y^2(y^q z-yz^q)+(z^2+kx^2)(z^q x-zx^q)=0\). Over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_q\), its projective Jacobian singular subscheme has exactly \(1+q(q+2)/4\) distinct support points, all on \(x\ne0\). At every such point the completed local algebra of the singular subscheme is \(\overline{\mathbb F}_q[[U,V]]/(U^2,V^2)\), of length four. The total singular-scheme length is \(q(q+2)+4\), independent of \(k\).

integrity.proof_basis: Symbolic Jacobian ideal, separable univariate polynomial of exact degree, formal local-parameter computation.

scientific_limitations: Geometric singular support and Jacobian scheme only; not analytic branch types, delta invariants, normalization or finite-field rationality of each singular point.
No assertion of irreducibility for individual parameter choices.
Possible overlap in more general literature on characteristic-two Frobenius curves remains a risk.
title: Uniform length-four singular-scheme thickening in the even-characteristic plane-filling family
